fields.v: Satisfaction distribution independent of task setting and CBA (chi-square = 2.74, p = 0.43); short-edit tasks slightly higher satisfaction. Authors state they do not directly compare interactions across CBAs. Met functional requirements correlate positively with satisfaction; non-executable code negatively (r = -0.24); developers mention correctness more than students (p = 0.034)

fields.v: Limitations: observer bias (think-aloud), small US sample, uncontrolled prior AI use, artificial short tasks, first prompt only, short-term lab setting, exploratory correlations. Gaps / design opportunities: guided prompting with clarifying questions (double-sided clarification), transparent and collaborative planning, hierarchical generation, self-verification plus user verification aids, restraint of proactive unsolicited changes, diff/PR-style change proposals with explanations, onboarding/teaching; future field, longitudinal and multi-round prompting studies

fields.v: Inconsistencies: abstract gives problem description in 48% and code structure in 48% of prompts (p. 1), while Table II gives problem description 0.56 (27/48) and file/modular structure 0.12 (6/48) (p. 4); abstract percentages for dissatisfaction factors (77%, 42%, 25%) not traceable in Table III (p. 1, 5); text r = 0.45 (p = 0.0015) for met functional requirements vs 0.34* in Table III (p. 5); implementation guidance 'r = -0.3' in text vs -0.37* in Table II (p. 4); text says unmet functional requirements in '16 of the 48 tasks (33%)' while Table III gives 16 mentions in 13 tasks (p. 5); 'Nine participants' on executability vs 9 mentions by 7 participants in Table III (p. 5-6); 'Of all seven readability-related statements, five ... while four ... The other two' adds up to eleven (Table III: 7 mentions) (p. 6); 'Five participants (P1, P5, P6, P8, P9, P16)' lists six (p. 7); two-way ANOVA F(1, 11) = 3.46 with p = 0.0004 is implausible (p. 7); two prompt types both labelled 'Type II' (p. 4); ignored context is called the 'primary and sole contributor' of poor maintainability with eleven participants listed (P1, P2, P4, P8-P10, P12-P16), while Table III gives poor maintainability 6 mentions in 6 tasks by 6 participants (p. 5, 7). Per-tool results only in Fig. 2. Supplementary material (tasks, prompts, interview protocol) at https://figshare.com/s/a13d7a90f13f2fcc2105 (p. 3, 11). IRB approved; no pre-registration. Programming languages: JavaScript and Python
